pcs.pc_description: Read and interpret the job sheet, work instructions, and SOPs to determine specifications such as product type, quantity, and program schedule.
Collect required materials like film or wire and cores from the store following organizational procedures.
Verify the availability and functionality of tools, machines, and safety equipment.
Inspect materials for any defects or inconsistencies before use.
Check the resistivity and quality of film or wire before use.
Fix wire terminals on the core and load the core on the shaft for manual or semi-automated systems.
Operate manual or semi-automated systems using updated control software and high-speed spindles by hand and pedal for precise winding.
Set up automated winding machines, load cores and film, and adjust rollers (pinch roller, traverse cutter, mill roller, guide rollers, tension roller) for wrinkle-free winding.
Configure advanced programmable winding machines with precision tools and digital interfaces, including winding cycle, resistance or capacitance, and material properties.
Operate the machine following the winding chart and ensure stable performance without wobbling.
Monitor and maintain ambient temperature, humidity, and contamination-free environments.
Ensure adherence to machine stop times and maintenance intervals as per manufacturer guidelines.

pcs.pc_description: Take samples of wound capacitors or resistors from each machine as per organizational guidelines.
Label and document the samples for traceability and future reference.
Record lot details of samples in the prescribed format or digital system.
Use capacitance or ohmmeters to measure and compare sample values against specifications.
Document variances and escalate issues to the supervisor.
Use digital multimeters, continuity testers, and advanced cable analyzers to check for capacitor shorts and measure resistivity.

modules.module_title: Undertake Preventive Maintenance of Winding Machine

pcs.pc_description: Perform regular cleaning of machines, equipment, and work areas as per manufacturer guidelines.
Inspect and calibrate tension controls, core settings, and sensors.
Synchronize rollers and adjust machine parameters to ensure smooth operation.
Identify and replace worn-out parts to prevent unexpected downtime.
Use predictive maintenance tools like vibration analyzers and thermal cameras to detect potential faults.
Maintain detailed logs of maintenance activities in digital systems.
Verify that windings meet specified ranges to avoid rejections.
Ensure timely delivery of symmetrical and defect-free windings to the next production stage.
Maintain records of outcomes, rejections, and corrective actions in compliance with organizational standards.
Implement continuous improvement practices to enhance productivity and quality.
Identify workplace hazards such as moving parts, electrical risks, or chemical fumes and follow safety signs and procedures.
Use appropriate personal protective equipment (PPE) like gloves, anti-static bands, and safety shoes; handle tools and components safely.
Identify fire hazards, use suitable fire extinguishers (Class A/B/C), and respond to fire emergencies with evacuation and rescue actions.
Administer first aid for injuries like burns, cuts, and shocks; follow emergency response protocols including evacuation and reporting.
Segregate recyclable, non-recyclable, and hazardous waste; dispose of materials like metals and plastics properly and maintain a clean workspace.
